fieldValues.title: Every decision names the boundary where it removes choices, and every agent records where decision flow stops
fieldValues.decision_question: When an agent meets a decision, what does it record so that we see the level where it matters, sense the domains we lack, and learn where decisions stop?
fieldValues.context: On 2026-10-28 the owner asked for a decision-flow section parallel to the work-flow map (vignettes 3e076051, 6606adfe, 5f271974, e3069d0d, 60d0e55c). Evidence: none of the 109 decisions in the programme log records its domain or level; 14 are design-kind technical choices in the strategy log (01cfb06e); 15 of 24 needs-input questions were already answered by principles (e832c6f4); decisions sit in at least seven stores with no index (finding 30c861a3). srs and srs-rust settle most choices by the decision compass and ADR-048 (41 of 54 rfc-decisions cite it); the programme has no equivalent in use. The section is container 68b6eb64-c628-4ea2-bf53-3e1051f6fe75 (six stages). Parallel to proposed decision fbba3d5e (work-flow stops).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
1. Do nothing: decisions keep no level. Leads to: technical choices keep reaching the owner, domains are guessed, decisions keep vanishing on a principle review only after reaching the owner.
2. Define the domain hierarchy first, then place decisions. Leads to: the problem moves to domain definition, which the owner rejects (vignette 5f271974).
3. Place every decision by boundary and record its stops (chosen). Leads to: a domain link where one exists, a plain boundary tag where none does; recurring boundaries are counted and proposed as domains; stops counted per stage.
4. A decisions server now. Leads to: one store, but built before the evidence that the index (remedy af3b7a6c) would give.
fieldValues.key_requirements: No domain is created just to place a decision; the boundary is named in plain words when no domain exists; recording never blocks the decision; repeats add evidence, not records.
fieldValues.decision_statement:
Placement. When any agent proposes, applies or finds a decision, its record names the boundary where it removes choices: a link to the domain when one exists, otherwise a tag boundary:<slug> naming the boundary in plain words. Shown above or beside its level (a strategy session, another group's desk), it is context there, not a decision to make.
Stops. When a decision vanished once a principle was applied, reached a level that is not its own, could not be found or lived only in a branch or PR text, was asked again, or was contradicted by practice, the agent records a com.semanticops.programme/finding in Suggestions, tagged decision-stop. The finding has dated evidence and evidences the stage of the decision flow (container 68b6eb64-c628-4ea2-bf53-3e1051f6fe75) where the decision stopped, and the problem behind it. A repeat of a known stop is added as evidence. Before escalating, the agent applies the compass and the recorded principles (remedy e120cf12).
Domains. A boundary tag that keeps recurring is brought to affirmation review as a candidate domain; domains whose decisions keep crossing are proposed for merging. Agents never create a domain to place a decision.
fieldValues.rationale: A decision removes choices only where it is relevant (owner, vignette 6606adfe). Naming the boundary at the point of decision costs a line and lets each level see only its own decisions; counting boundaries and stops senses the domains and the failure points from experience instead of designing them first.
fieldValues.revisit_when: After a month: boundary tags do not converge, or decision-stop findings are rare while the owner still receives decisions below their level. Or the index shows losses a decisions server would prevent.
fieldValues.next_steps: Handbook text beside Recording where flow stops; a pointer in the srs-context brief; the decision index (remedy af3b7a6c) as a clerk issue; existing decisions are placed as they are next cited.
